title: Programming Languages & Paradigms Track
description: Rigorous progression across programming language theory, type systems, and the major paradigms from low-level systems (Assembly, C, Rust) to OOP, Functional (Haskell, Lisp), Logic, and Concurrent systems (Go).

steps.note: Hardware execution foundation: registers, ALU, memory hierarchy, and instruction cycles.
Architecture-specific instruction sets, stack frames, calling conventions, and register allocation.
Procedural systems programming: pointer arithmetic, manual memory layout, and ABI kernel interfaces.
Type theory foundations: lambda calculus, Hindley-Milner type inference, and typing soundness proofs.
Modern systems safety: affine types, ownership, borrow checking, and zero-cost abstractions.
Multi-paradigm abstractions: RAII, smart pointers, templates, and compile-time metaprogramming.
Managed OOP runtime: JVM bytecode execution, class loaders, and generational garbage collection.
Pure functional paradigm: non-strict lazy evaluation, typeclasses, and monadic I/O abstractions.
Homoiconic symbolic computation: S-expressions, lexical closures, and macro metaprogramming.
Declarative logic programming: Horn clauses, Robinson resolution, and unification search.
Dynamic multi-paradigm runtime: data models, generators, dynamic dispatch, and C extensions.
Event-driven asynchronous web execution combined with static structural type checking.
Scalable concurrency: Communicating Sequential Processes (CSP), goroutines, and message-passing channels.
